h: Choosing the Path Whose Suffering Ends in Light

p: בְּסִפְרֵי רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (סִפְרֵי דְּבָרִים נג)
In the Sifrei at the beginning of this parshah (Sifrei Devarim 53):
that you may live, you and your offspring."
A parable: a man was sitting
and before him were two paths,
one whose beginning was level ground
and one whose beginning was thorns
and whose end was level ground.
And he would inform the passersby,
and in the end you come out among thorns;
and in the end you come out on level ground."
they prosper in this world, etc.;
when they suffer in this world
for two or three days they suffer,
and in the end they rejoice," etc.
Now, he took as his parable
כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (עֵירוּבִין נג, ב)
similar to what they said in the Gemara (Eruvin 53b)
But there the gardens and orchards
and he did not see them
until he had walked the whole way,
but here, where he took in the parable
is this not visible to every person,
what will be at the end of his way
So what did this come to teach him?
אַךְ נִרְאֶה שֶׁתָּפַס ב׳ וְג׳ פְּסִיעוֹת
But it seems he took two or three steps
where he said of the wicked
שֶׁמַּצְלִיחִים ב׳ וְג׳ יָמִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
that they prosper two or three days in this world,
that they suffer two or three days
At first glance this is not understood:
is it only for two or three days
that "the way of the wicked prospers"
הֲלֹא כָּל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִתְנַהֵג כֵּן
Is not all of this world conducted so,
the reward for the mitzvos they do in this world,
and there are those all of whose days are like festivals?
And likewise the reverse with the righteous,
for light sins in this world
there are those who suffer all their days
as is known that the six days of Creation
and the day of the Holy One, blessed be He,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ מִמַּה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (מִשְׁלֵי ח, ל)
As they expounded from what is said (Mishlei 8:30):
"And I was a delight day after day"
that the Torah preceded by two thousand years
לִבְרִיאַת עוֹלָם (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יט, א)
the creation of the world (Vayikra Rabbah 19:1);
and they allude to Chochmah and Binah,
the seven sefiros of the structure,
which are the seven days of Creation.
And likewise teshuvah, which is the aspect of Binah,
כַּיָּדוּעַ שֶׁהֵם כְּנֶגֶד חֶסֶד גְּבוּרָה תִּפְאֶרֶת
as is known that they correspond to Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferes.
Now, the destruction of the First Temple
was in the year 338 of the fourth millennium
and it is stated in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 97b):
and in the last jubilee the son of David will come";
and this was the year 250 of the fifth millennium,
that is, in the generation of the later Amoraim.
And likewise the end that was calculated
רַב סַעְדְיָה גָּאוֹן וְרַשִׁ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
by Rav Saadiah Gaon and Rashi, of blessed memory,
was also in the fifth millennium.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מָצָאנוּ קִיצִּים בָּאֶלֶף הַשִּׁשִּׁי
Afterward we find dates for the end in the sixth millennium,
at the time of our masters
הָאֲרִיזַ״ל וְהַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
the Arizal and the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory,
when the salvation would be more complete.
And likewise in the year 338 of the sixth millennium,
when two thousand years were completed
from the destruction of the First Temple,
was the time of the spread
of the teaching of the holy Ari, of blessed memory.
And this is why he took in the lesson
that is, in the fourth millennium
that is, when the end will be in the sixth millennium,
in the fourth, fifth and sixth millennia.
But in the end they rejoice at the last;
and he brought several pesukim on this,
"to do you good at your end";
טוֹב אַחֲרִית דָּבָר וְגוֹמֵר (קֹהֶלֶת ז, ח)
"Better is the end of a thing," etc. (Koheles 7:8);
That is, in the Babylonian exile
and as has been explained several times.
that was hidden away for the righteous,
as they said (in the holy Zohar in many places);
וְהוּא נִגְנַז לַעֲמֵלֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and it was hidden away for those who toil in the Oral Torah,
the light created on the first day, etc.
And the main reason for the length of this exile
is in order to bring out
that is, that all the light
of the Oral Torah should spread.
"The path of the righteous is like the shining light,"
and the end of the pasuk:
"that shines ever brighter until the full day";
that is, that all the light should spread
so that they merit the spreading
that is stored for those who toil in the Oral Torah.
